absent: Hash entry computation and removal path for resource counters beyond insertion.
Full child sysctl registration sequence and failure handling for new user namespaces.
Credential allocation and installation semantics used during helper startup.
Exact signal disposition reset and program launch behavior for helper threads.
Scheduling and lifetime guarantees for helper work items and their parent linkage.
Concurrent traversal and reference rules for the namespace tree during deferred free.
Overflow identifier values for user and group translations and their exposure policy.
Epoll accounting interactions for user objects and their error paths.
Counter limit enforcement points where the configured maxima are consulted.
Freeze handling and preemption rules around the helper gate wait loops.

findings.text: Releases per user namespace sysctl state by unregistering the registered table and retiring the associated set and freeing the backing table memory when sysctl support is present.

Provides a read biased gate around helper execution with an interruptible try variant that reports full disable distinctly plus a bounded uninterruptible wait variant plus an unlock plus a direct depth install plus a draining disable that waits for in flight helpers before succeeding.
Offers registration and unregistration of per task return hooks backed by a per CPU list plus a firing routine that invokes every hook currently queued on the local CPU during return to user mode.

Emulates multiprocessor callouts on a single CPU build by invoking the supplied routine directly with interrupts masked and preemption controlled while validating the target CPU and optionally pinning the virtual CPU around the call.
Translates project identifiers between namespace local values and kernel global values in both directions with a munged variant that substitutes a designated overflow value when no mapping exists.

Defers user namespace teardown to process context and then iteratively removes each namespace from the global tree and releases extended mapping storage and retires sysctls and key state and frees through deferred reclaim and accounts the namespace count and continues up the parent chain while references drop.
Exposes legacy narrow width wrappers for ownership and identity changes that widen narrow arguments to full width before delegating to the native implementation.
Exposes legacy narrow width query wrappers that translate kernel identifiers to the calling namespace and narrow them for legacy width and copy results to user memory with size validation.
Sysctl lookup and visibility for resource counters always resolve to the set owned by the current user namespace so each namespace observes only its own controls.

Permission computation for counter controls derives a single access digit from the table mode using owner rights for resource control capability holders and other read rights otherwise then replicates that digit across all access classes.

The initial user namespace maps the entire unsigned range identically in all three identity maps with one extent each and is owned by global root user and group and carries the initial flag set plus default keyring and misc handler state where configured.
The root identity object starts with a single pinned reference and is inserted into the hash at cache init after accounting for it succeeds.

Writes to helper capability controls intersect the existing mask with the supplied value under lock so controls can only lose privileges and never gain them while reads present the current mask as a pair of narrow words with low part first.

Extent matching treats a request as contained only when both its first and last identifiers fall inside the same extent in the direction selected by the key while ordering earlier ranges before and later ranges after.
Unmapped project identifier queries collapse to a single overflow value rather than leaking the internal failure sentinel.
The sixteen bit compatibility header is protected by a single inclusion guard macro.
The user namespace slab cache pointer is writeable only during early init and treated as read only thereafter.
Insertion of freshly allocated resource counters into the hash is serialized by an interrupt masking spin guard held only across the hash link step.
Both helper capability masks share one small spin guard that is held for sampling during helper startup and for sampling plus narrowing during sysctl access.
The global user hash uses an interrupt masking spin guard around insertion of the initial root entry during cache init with the table preinitialized to empty buckets.

The helper disabled state and its wait queue are protected by a read write semaphore taken for read by execution gates and for write by state installers allowing concurrent readers but exclusive writers.
Helper startup serializes clearing of inherited signal handling with the target sighand lock and then normalizes filesystem mask and scheduling priority before installing credentials.
User namespace state changes are serialized by a dedicated mutex.

Counter limit controls share a uniform descriptor carrying a textual name plus a long sized length plus a world readable mode plus a bounded integer vector handler plus pointers to zero and maximum bounds.
The counter sysctl root binds a lookup operation tied to current namespace and a permission operation tied to namespace capability evaluation.

Helper capability controls expose two entries for bounding and inheritable masks each holding a pointer to the live mask plus a two word length plus an owner only mode plus a shared capability handler.
Map search keys carry a direction selector plus a starting identifier plus a length describing the range under test.
The initial miscellaneous binary handler starts enabled with an empty entry list and a statically unlocked guard.

The initial namespace object aggregates common namespace state plus three single extent maps plus owner and group plus flags plus optional keyring list with semaphore plus a pointer to the initial misc handler.

The user hash size and mask derive from a conditional bit count that selects a smaller table on constrained builds with a mixing function combining shifted and unshifted identifier bits under the mask backed by a slab cache and a static bucket array.
Completion handoff uses an atomic exchange of the waiter pointer to decide ownership completing the waiter when present and otherwise releasing the request block directly.

Helper launch separates a waiting path that runs synchronously and reaps the child from a non waiting path that reparents to the core thread for automatic reaping with the async starter reporting its status for the waiter to consume or completing immediately when no waiter exists.

Helper gating moves between enabled and nested disabled depths parking new entrants on a queue while disabled with interruptible entrants able to observe the fully disabled level distinctly and draining disable restoring enabled state when the quiesce interval expires.
Namespace teardown iterates from the released object up through parents while each parent reference drops to zero performing tree removal and resource release at every step.
The per task user return flag is set on first registration on the local CPU and cleared only when the last entry is removed so firing occurs solely while the list is non empty.
Legacy narrow width system calls provide user entry for ownership changes plus identity changes plus group list management plus identity queries.
Early initialization registers the top level user sysctl directory and child controls plus creates the user cache and hashes root plus registers helper capability controls.
Group list conversion validates size bounds and privilege before allocation then fails the whole operation on any user copy fault or unmappable identifier while releasing the temporary buffer.
Disable requests with an empty depth are rejected and a drain that does not observe quiescence within the bounded interval restores enabled state and reports contention rather than remaining blocked.
Negative wait intervals are rejected without sleeping and single CPU dispatch rejects any target other than the boot CPU without invoking the routine.
Capability control writes require both privilege management and module control capabilities rejecting unprivileged writers before any state is examined.
Legacy identifier queries translate each of three credentials under the caller namespace and propagate the first user store failure while still attempting the defined order.
Helper drain patience spans five seconds expressed in clock ticks.

Counter controls use mode 0644 and are sized as native long with lower bound zero and upper bound taken from the maximum signed integer covering per namespace limits for standard namespaces and optional subsystem counts where configured.
Helper capability nodes use mode 0600 and are sized as two native unsigned words presented low part first.
User hash uses three bits on constrained builds and seven bits otherwise yielding eight or one hundred twenty eight buckets with mask one less than size.
Initial identity maps each contain one extent starting at zero mapping the full unsigned range.
Helper control starts in fully disabled depth with zero running helpers and helper masks start fully set.
Group set size is bounded above by the global maximum group count and negative query sizes are rejected.
Helper startup resets the file creation mask to 0022 and resets scheduling priority to neutral.
